svg.title: Loop flipbook · the layers of a running LLM system, lit one at a time
svg.desc: Animated flipbook in a 16:9 frame. On the left, the loop number and a green card, separate from the structure, naming the focused layer and giving what it is and how you see it. On the right, Figure 1's layers. At the top: training (a bar, which sets the weights), the model, and the model safeguards strip, set by whoever runs the model. Below them, the run: the environment (what the tools can reach), holding the harness, which holds the context, the operator controls and the tools the operator controls permit; the harness calls the model and receives its response; monitors (a vertical strip) observe the run from outside; governance (a band at the bottom) sets every layer, with lines up to the environment, the monitors, the model safeguards and training. Left of the run, a thin user-interface column lists the ways a person or outside party reaches the harness, top to bottom: chat tool, code tool, API, other; a two-way arrow joins it to the harness. Eleven loops, from the user interface (0) through governance (10), each bring one more part into focus, in this order: user interface, then model, training, model safeguards, then context, harness, operator controls, tools, environment, monitors, governance. A dotted brass line runs from the card to the focused layer. A focused part fills blue and carries the loop number; earlier parts settle to a lighter blue and keep their numbers. The final frame has every layer, the user-interface column included, coloured and numbered, and the card reads “All layers. Every layer has a part.” The markup as stored shows that final frame.

g.text: the weights · keeps nothing between calls
set by whoever runs the model
Governance· the people and policy that set every layer

g.data-live: Loop 0, User interface. What it is: The feature a human or outside party uses to interact with an AI system built on a large language model. How you see it: The chat window where you type a prompt or attach a file, or, for coding, enter detailed instructions, and where the response appears.
Loop 1, Model. What it is: The trained weights. It does nothing until it is called. How you see it: It reads your prompt, plus the rest of the context, and writes the reply you see.

Loop 2, Training. What it is: Sets the weights so the model makes its best prediction, including what it learns to refuse. How you see it: How the model responds, how accurate or useful the reply is, and which requests it turns down.

Loop 3, Model safeguards. What it is: Filters, classifiers and account enforcement that the vendor, such as Anthropic or OpenAI, runs around the model. How you see it: Ask for help getting around a security feature and you may get a warning or a blocked request.
Loop 4, Context. What it is: Everything the model is shown, every call. How you see it: What you type or attach, plus the thread's earlier messages. In a long thread, early details drop out.

Loop 5, Harness. What it is: The program that runs the loop: it builds the context from your prompts and the replies, and controls access to the web, email or documents. How you see it: The app that searches the web, runs code the model wrote, or reads your files or email and passes them to the model.

Loop 6, Operator controls. What it is: Settings that decide what runs without asking you first. How you see it: A coding assistant asking "Allow this command?", or a chat app asking to reach your email or Google Drive. In some tools, the choice between automatic and manual approval.

Loop 7, Tools. What it is: The actions the harness can take for the model: search the web, read and write files, run code, send email. How you see it: "Searching the web…" in the app, or the connectors you switch on.
Loop 8, Execution environment. What it is: Where the tools run, and what they can reach: files, network, services. How you see it: Whether it can open your files and browse, or only talk.
Loop 9, Monitors. What it is: Watchers outside the run that can alert or stop it. How you see it: Mostly invisible; you would only see a run stopped.

g.text: run that can alert or stop

g.data-live: Loop 10, Governance. What it is: The people and policy that set the controls on every layer. How you see it: Your plan's usage policy, your company admin's settings, and what you let an agent reach or change.
